newsitem.title: EGYPT: Cements, banks firm Egypt share prices.
newsitem.headline: Cements, banks firm Egypt share prices.

text.p: Cement and banking sector gains breathed new life into Egyptian share prices on Tuesday with brokers saying the days of profit taking after record highs have come to an end.
The all-share Capital Market Authority index rose a small 1.39 points to 396.89 points, a move which brokers said was a great leap for the slumbering market.
Volume was an average 78.18 million pounds ($22.99 million), down from Monday's heavy 107.3 million.
"The market is looking good price-wise and tomorrow it's going to be even better. The prices are now attractive," said broker Yasser Darwish from El-Rashad Securities Brokerage.
Millers, realty firms and the blue-chip banks and cements still topped daily turnover but the most volume came from recently privatised Nile Cotton Ginning.
Brokers said mutual funds selling their stakes in the firm to each other probably generated the 21.54 million pounds volume and the stock closed 3.37 pounds up at 70.88.
Both Commercial International Bank (CIB) and Misr International Bank/MIBANK were their sectors most active, but ended mixed.

CIB closed 4.67 pounds up at 98.22 a day after brokers said the bank split its shares 10 for one while MIBANK ended 18 pounds lower 792 with its global depositary receipt offering roadshow in progress.
Other gainers included Egyptian American Bank which rose 3 to 170 in busy trade.

Brokers said the firmer cement shares helped offset the continued losses in the milling sector which has been the most hit by profit taking. Suez Cement rose one pound to 32 while Egyptian Portland Tora Cement gained 1.45 to 95.45.
South Cairo Flour Mills nosedived 3.99 to 75.91 and Central and West Delta Flour Mills fell 0.99 to 105.01.

Cairo Housing and Development was also active with 17.79 million pounds of trading and rose 1.17 to 24.72. The state has offered a 20 percent stake in the firm and brokers said investors were trying to get in on the privatisation.
The index for openly traded firms rose to 648.31 from 631.42 points on Monday and the index for rarely traded "closed" firms fell to 265.25 from 266.76 points.
Out of the 86 shares traded, 32 gained, 31 lost and 23 ended the day unchanged.
